page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.16xlarge is a dedicated memory-optimized server powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-N1 processor. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the instance provides 64 physical cores mapped directly to 64 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 1024 GB of RAM, equating to an expansive 16 GB of memory per core. Bundled storage consists of 3800 GB of integrated NVMe SSD instance storage, complemented by a 25 Gbps baseline networking interface. No GPU accelerators are configured on this server.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-threaded execution and high memory throughput alongside distinct single-thread limitations. The server achieves top-quartile results in multi-core stress-ng tests (97052.9) and software compilation using Clang (42973.0). It demonstrates exceptional key-value caching performance, processing 72.65 million Redis SET operations per second backed by 3783.24 GB/sec in cached small-block memory bandwidth. In contrast, single-core processing capabilities are modest, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 968.0 and lower-tier throughput in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression. Large language model text generation also registers low throughput across various parameter sizes.

The physical core density and 1 TB memory capacity present a cost-effective infrastructure profile for memory-bound services compared to standard compute instances. By coupling substantial memory density with 3800 GB of fast local NVMe storage, it eliminates the need for expensive multi-node scaling when hosting high-volume memory workloads. The instance is suited for large in-memory key-value stores, distributed Redis caching tiers, real-time analytics engines, and parallelized CI/CD build environments.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-core ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each vCPU maps to a dedicated physical core without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 1024 GB of system memory to achieve a high 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is provided via 3800 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network capability. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core scaling in stress-ng and compiler tasks, as well as outstanding in-memory Redis SET performance reaching 72.65 million operations per second. However, single-threaded processing and LLM text generation metrics rank in lower percentiles. The hardware architecture offers efficient resource density for applications requiring substantial memory footprints without demanding high per-thread burst speeds. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, real-time analytics, and data processing pipelines.
